plan.summary: Part 3 of 4. Synopsis sweep (BRO-4853, owner request 2026-10-07). Other Desert Cities carried a false Tony claim copied from Show Score; a site-wide audit (regex detectors plus a whole-corpus model sweep, every hit read by hand) found 70 more bad synopses: Fela! (1776 text), The Great Society (Great Comet text), 5 cookie-banner records, and 63 records holding another work's Wikipedia article, a person's biography, a disambiguation page, a song list or wiki markup.
steps: Rewrite the Other Desert Cities (2026), Fela! and The Great Society synopses from sourced facts
Clear the 63 wrong-article synopses so the production-verified enricher can refill them

actions.oldValue: "Doctor Jazz" is a popular tune and song written by Joe "King" Oliver in 1926. Publisher Walter Melrose got his name on it as co-composer, as was often his practice. It enjoyed its initial popularity in the 1920s. It continues to be played by Dixieland jazz groups. It has been performed by many notable acts, such as Jelly Roll Morton, Chris Barber, Harry Connick Jr.

actions.oldValue: Savinien de Cyrano de Bergerac ( , ; 6 March 1619 – 28 July 1655) was a French novelist, playwright, epistolarian, and duelist. A bold and innovative author, his work was part of the libertine literature of the first half of the 17th century. Today, he is best known as the inspiration for Edmond Rostand's most noted drama, Cyrano de Bergerac (1897), which, although it includes elements of his life, also contains invention and myth.

actions.oldValue:
"Beauty and the Beast" is a fairy tale written by the French novelist Gabrielle-Suzanne Barbot de Villeneuve and published anonymously in 1740 in La Jeune Américaine et les contes marins (The Young American and Marine Tales).
Villeneuve's original story was abridged, revised, and published by French novelist Jeanne-Marie Leprince de Beaumont in 1756 in Magasin des enfants (Children's Collection) which became the most commonly retold version.

In particular, in the American Chess the entire show is about one chess match, not two. Act 1 involves the first part of the match, which is held in Bangkok, Thailand, while Act 2 handles the conclusion, and is set in Budapest, Hungary.
